clue.text: Festive polka he'd danced, an unexpected turn-up

indicators.note: letters that have danced have moved about, so the words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: At a Christmas party someone dances a polka, which surprises everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'danced' rearranges the fifteen letters of FESTIVE POLKA HED.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is said when a person who was just being discussed suddenly arrives, a surprise appearance.

clue.text: Entering police speed trap, one gets nearer

indicators.note: one thing entering another goes inside it, so the numeral goes into the police device

parts.note: a Stinger is the spiked strip British police lay across a road to stop a speeding car
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone drives into a police speed trap and gets closer to the camera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearer' is the old sense of near meaning mean with money, not closer in distance.
explanation.definitionFit: Near can mean tight-fisted, so nearer is the comparative of mean with money.

clue.text: Dreadful-sounding colourist

indicators.note: sounding tells us to take the word as it is heard spoken, not as spelt

parts.note: dreadful means dire

explanation.surface: A hairdresser's colouring work is terrible.
explanation.definitionFit: A person whose trade is dyeing cloth or hair gives things their colour.

clue.text: Type of sporting grey coat

indicators.note: sporting suggests the letters play about and take a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Asking what kind of athletic grey jacket someone wears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sporting' rearranges the letters of GREY COAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A type is a class or kind of thing, a grouping synonym.

clue.text: Red line covers a page in centre of worship

indicators.note: the outer pieces cover the inner ones, so they wrap around the letters for the article and page

parts.note: Che Guevara was a famous red, a revolutionary communist

explanation.surface: A newspaper's red-ink line is printed over a page in the middle of a worship guide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red' is not a colour here but a communist, the revolutionary Che Guevara.
explanation.definitionFit: A chapel is a small building or room set aside for Christian services, a place of prayer.

clue.text: Diplomat's car back shortly

parts.note: the Mini is a classic British small car

indicators.note: shortly means the word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: the stern is the back of a ship

explanation.surface: An ambassador's car will soon be back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' trims STERN to STER.
explanation.definitionFit: A minister is a diplomatic envoy ranking below an ambassador.

clue.text: Male creature and baby get much more intense

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep
a pup is a baby animal, such as a young dog or seal

explanation.surface: An adult male animal and its young grow fiercer.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to increase or intensify quickly, as with production or pressure.

clue.text: Arrogant, having an IQ of 150?

definitions.meaning: describes someone whose show of cleverness is irritatingly smug
taking 100 as average, 150 is that level plus a further half again

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is literal: an IQ of 150 is average intelligence exceeded by one half.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone annoyingly smart in a show-off way; literally, 150 is 100 plus a half.

clue.text: Typecast in play, initially hope for change

indicators.note: letters in play are being moved around, so they are rearranged
initially picks the first letter of the word hope

explanation.surface: An actor typecast in a play hopes for a change of role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in play' rearranges TYPECAST into PETTYCAS; 'initially' adds the H of hope.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the small fund of coins and notes kept in an office for minor expenses, loose money.

clue.text: Away from the borders, raid a hostile state

indicators.note: taking letters away from the borders of the phrase leaves its inner part, here sitting within the words

explanation.surface: A raid strikes a hostile country far from its frontiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Idaho is one of the states of the USA, in the northwest.

clue.text: Chair here (own Scots pine, for example)

parts.note: ain is the Scots word for own
a pine is an example of a tree

explanation.surface: A piece of furniture made from Scottish pine of your own.
explanation.walkthrough: The Chair is a famous fence on the Grand National course at Aintree, the racecourse near Liverpool.
explanation.definitionFit: The racecourse where the Grand National is run has a big jump called the Chair.

clue.text: Oversexed pair flopping with film

indicators.note: flopping suggests the letters fall about into a new order

parts.note: pic is informal for a film

explanation.surface: A lustful couple fail with their movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flopping' rearranges PAIR to PRIA.
explanation.definitionFit: From Priapus, the Greek fertility god, the adjective means phallic or lecherous.

clue.text: Poet in old film

parts.note: vid is short for video, a film

explanation.surface: A poet appears in an old movie.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovid was the Roman writer of the Metamorphoses.

clue.text: One could get fleeced here in court — lawyers principally stick together

parts.note: to court someone is to woo them

indicators.note: principally picks the first letter of the word lawyers

parts.note: to staple is to fasten together

explanation.surface: A defendant is robbed in court, where lawyers mainly stick together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fleeced' looks like being cheated by lawyers; here it is a sheep's coat being traded.
explanation.definitionFit: A wool staple was a historical market town authorised for the trade in sheep fleeces.

clue.text: Careful of the short gap at end of runway

indicators.note: short means the word is cut, losing its last letter

parts.note: a rift is a gap or crack

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of runway

explanation.surface: Taking care over the small space at the end of an airstrip.
explanation.definitionFit: Being careful with money means spending it economically, not wastefully.

clue.text: Non-contributory benefit for railway staff?

definitions.meaning: something gained without paying one's share
train workers would literally travel without paying

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means getting something without paying for it, and literally a journey taken at no cost.

clue.text: Understand about opening heart in solemn procession

indicators.note: opening means splitting another word to sit inside it

parts.note: the core is the heart of something

indicators.note: about tells us to turn the word round

parts.note: to get something is to understand it

explanation.surface: Grasping how a heart operation goes during a funeral.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses the synonym for Understand before it opens up the heart.
explanation.definitionFit: A cortège is a funeral procession, a slow ceremonial line of mourners.

clue.text: Insistent solicitors are cold with people displaying emotion

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
huggers are people who show affection by embracing

explanation.surface: Pushy lawyers are frosty towards emotional people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'solicitors' suggests British lawyers, but it means people soliciting donations; chuggers are charity fundraisers who stop shoppers in the street.
explanation.definitionFit: Charity muggers pressure passers-by on the street to sign up for donations, persistent askers.

clue.text: Waste energy on coat I took in

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for energy in physics
a mac is a raincoat, short for mackintosh
to take food in is to eat; ate is the past tense

explanation.surface: Someone frets about wasting effort on a coat they altered.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to waste away means to become thin; this verb means to make or become very thin.

clue.text: Team given extra exam

parts.note: a cricket or football side has eleven players
a plus is something additional

explanation.surface: A sports side has been given an additional test.
explanation.walkthrough: This is the British exam once taken at about age 11 to decide entry to grammar schools.
explanation.definitionFit: The test children sat in their last primary year to select for grammar schools.

clue.text: Blame for spilling marmalade, just having opened preserve

indicators.note: spilling suggests letters tipped out and landing in a new order
something just opened shows only its first letter, so take the initial of marmalade

explanation.surface: Someone blames another for spilling marmalade from a jar of preserves just opened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spilling' rearranges BLAME into EMBAL; 'just having opened' adds the M of marmalade.
explanation.definitionFit: To embalm a body is to keep it from decay with chemicals.

clue.text: Speed effortlessly through part, not needing this?

indicators.note: one word passing through another sits inside it

parts.note: to romp is to win or move along easily

explanation.surface: An actor sails through a role without needing help.
explanation.walkthrough: An actor who knows the part needs no cue from the wings, so the definition leans on the whole clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A prompt is the whispered line fed to an actor who has forgotten their words.

clue.text: Greta's short dress

indicators.note: short means the name is cut, losing its last letter

parts.note: Greta Garbo was the Swedish film star

explanation.surface: A woman named Greta's little frock.
explanation.definitionFit: Garb is clothing, an outfit or costume.

clue.text: This thus inhibiting business graduate?

indicators.note: inhibiting means holding in or restraining, so one word holds the other inside it

parts.note: ergo is Latin for therefore, thus
an MBA is a Master of Business Administration

explanation.surface: Something that hampers a holder of a business degree.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue describes a trade ban hampering business people.
explanation.definitionFit: An embargo is an official ban on trade with a country, restricting commerce.

clue.text: Fish dish, head removed, filled with new parsley, perhaps

indicators.note: the outer pieces are filled with a letter put inside them

parts.note: a gar is a long-snouted fish

indicators.note: head removed means the first letter is taken off

parts.note: taken as written before losing its first letter

explanation.surface: A fish course topped with fresh parsley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fish dish' looks like one item; 'Fish' gives its own piece and 'dish' loses its head.
explanation.definitionFit: Parsley is an example of a decorative herb placed on food.

clue.text: Speaking plainly, not top level

indicators.note: in a down entry, not top means losing the first letter

parts.note: frank means candid and direct

explanation.surface: An honest remark about someone not quite at the top grade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not top level' looks like one phrase; 'not top' is the deletion and 'level' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A rank is a grade or position in a hierarchy.

clue.text: Turned over papers by the light

parts.note: ID means identity papers
an LED is a light-emitting diode

explanation.surface: Someone flicked through documents next to a lamp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned over' suggests flipping pages, but it is an engine ticking over.
explanation.definitionFit: An engine that turns over is running without engaging gear.

clue.text: Around time of arrival of train, leap out

indicators.note: out signals the letters are taken apart and put in a different order

explanation.surface: As a train arrives someone jumps out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges TRAIN and LEAP; 'arrival' means a baby's birth, not a train's.
explanation.definitionFit: The medical adjective describes the weeks just before and after birth.
